newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian shares consolidate ahead of expiry.
newsitem.headline: Belgian shares consolidate ahead of expiry.

text.p: Mild profit-taking took the bourse mostly lower on Friday as players awaited the monthly expiry of futures and options later in the session.
Traders said it was hard to predict whether the derivatives settlement would push the Bel-20 index .BFX back up towards its record high hit on Thursday or deepen the correction.
"Last month we expected the market to go down a lot, but we saw a lot of (Bel-20) baskets (bought) at the end," one trader commented. "It's very difficult to say what will happen."
By mid-morning, the Bel-20 was 0.35 percent lower at 2,532.41 points, well off Thursday's 2,562.94 life high.
Monday's market holiday in Belgium was another factor weighing on prices, one dealer added.

Recent market darling UCB was the main loser. The chemicals and drugs group was down 2.29 percent at 145,100 francs. Chemicals maker Solvay, which denied rumours on Thursday it was interested in buying UCB, was up 0.68 percent at 22,050 francs.
One trader said UCB's fall had more to do with profit-taking than Solvay's denial. "Solvay's denial was not news to us," one trader said. "But we still don't know who was buying (UCB)."
